content.title: New 2027 Social Security COLA Projections Announced
content.text: When we say projections, we mean projections, and it’s still anyone’s guess. The actual number is months away, but for those who like to be prepared, there are at least two new projections for the 2027 Social Security COLA increase to choose from. The Bureau of Labor Statistics has just reported a current inflation rate of 2.4% — relatively modest, in line with expectations, matching last month’s reading, and certainly not reflecting recent headlines (those will pretty much all tell you that inflation is going to go higher). That said, as a result, the Senior Citizens League is now predicting a Social Security COLA of 2.8% — as it did a month ago, matching the actual 2026 COLA. They use a model that incorporates the Consumer Price Index, the Federal Reserve interest rate, and the national unemployment rate to make its predictions. Meanwhile, independent analyst Mary Johnson[i] now predicts/projects 1.7%, up from 1.2% a month earlier. That’s quite a bit lower than in recent years, when inflation was higher. In 2022 and 2023, the COLAs were 5.9% and 8.7%, respectively, both the highest in four decades. Of course, the actual cost-of-living adjustment will be based on the increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI-W) from the third quarter of 2025 through the third quarter of 2026. Which is to say that it’s going to be a while before we have a good sense of what it might wind up being. One might argue, of course, that such a projection is a bit fanciful, considering how much time — and how many events — stand between today and when that actual COLA is determined. But why wait till the last minute to click? [i] a Social Security and Medicare policy analyst, writer, and editor of The Social Security and Medicare Advisor newsletter for The Senior Citizens League.
